'''''Star Wars: Imperial Handbook''''', stylized as '''''Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide''''', is a [[2014]] [[Legends]] guidebook written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and published by [[becker&mayer!]]. The book is in the style of [[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide|an in-universe book]] on the procedures and tactical guidelines for the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]]. It is bundled with a motorized case with lights and sounds, an introductory note from [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], and a specially designed die-cast Imperial military medal. The book is also available by itself.

Pre-orders were supposed to start on [[July 1]], 2014. However, a customer-service message from becker&mayer! later implied that the book would be available for pre-order on their website around [[September 1]].<ref name="Customer Service message">{{JCFCite|url=posts/51687725|board=Literature|thread=Imperial Handbook – A Commander's Guide|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802144732/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/imperial-handbook-a-commanders-guide.50019488/page-11}}</ref> It was released on [[October 14]], 2014.<ref name="Amazon" />

==Publisher's summary==
''As the Galactic Empire expands, high-ranking officials from each branch of the Imperial Military have set down tactical guidelines and procedures for all newly ascending commanders. Set in-universe, this compendium of ordinance, mission reports, and Imperial philosophy was intercepted by members of the Rebel Alliance, some of whom also left commentary scribbled in the margins. Housed in a deluxe case that opens with lights and sounds, this never-before-seen Imperial Handbook is perfect for ''Star Wars'' fans—no matter which side of the Civil War they're on.''<ref name="TheForce.net" />

==Development==
In [[2019]], 3D artist [[Ansel Hsiao]], known for his work in ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', complained that some of the artworks published on his [http://fractalsponge.net website] were reused without his consent by the illustrator [[Joe Corroney]] in ''Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide''.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://http://fractalsponge.net/?p=4224|text=Hey, Disney and Joe Corroney|author=[[Ansel Hsiao|Hsiao, Ansel]]|date=2019-02-16|archivedate=20190224032232}}</ref><ref>{{ArtStation|username=fractalsponge|url=fractalsponge/blog/wAWe/turns-out-desaturate-in-photoshop-is-great|name=[[Ansel Hsiao]]|text=Turns out, desaturate in Photoshop is great.}}</ref>

==Continuity==
Although it was released after April 2014's split of the [[canon]]/[[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuities and the creation of the rule that any works released after that date are to be designated canon, becker&mayer! has confirmed that the ''Imperial Handbook'' is branded as ''Star Wars'' Legends, meaning it is not part of the current canon.<ref name="Facebook">{{Facebook|username=beckermayerbooks|url=beckermayerbooks/posts/865867973431390|name=[[becker&mayer!|Becker&mayer! Books]]|date=2014-09-12|quote=Hi Mark! Imperial Handbook is set in Legends.|archivefile=File:BeckerMayer-ImperialHandbookLegends-Facebook.png|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: Does anyone know if this book is set in Legends? Or Canon?}}</ref> Despite this, it does have references to canon material, such as the [[Lasan Suppression]], the [[All Terrain Defense Pod/Legends|AT-DP]] and the [[TIE Advanced prototype]].<ref name="SWIHACG" /> The propaganda posters ''[[Strength & Obedience]]'', ''[[COMPNOR Recruitment]]'', and ''[[Expose, Pursue, Destroy]]'' were also later reused in the [[2016]] canon reference book ''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' (although the last one was slightly modified when it later appeared in canon).<ref name="Propaganda">''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]''</ref>
